findings.message: A callback rejection after effect authorization is classified unable-to-proceed even though the atomic effect may have occurred; retrying without checkpoint reconciliation could duplicate or overwrite work.
The returned effectResult is inserted directly into a deep-frozen Core outcome, freezing adapter-owned data rather than an isolated Core copy.

requiredCorrections: After applyAtomicConditionalEffect has been called, catch/rejection/normalization failure must return an explicit effect-uncertain outcome containing the exact invocation and a non-authoritative diagnostic; it must never return unable-to-proceed or imply zero effect.
Keep unable-to-proceed only for failures proven to occur before effect authorization, such as invalid input or observation failure.
Clone JSON-compatible effect results before embedding and deep-freezing them; prove the callback's original object remains mutable and is not shared with the Core result.

Add tests for callback rejection after a simulated mutation, effect-result clone isolation, and continued zero-call behavior for every pre-effect failure while retaining all concurrency and drift coverage.
